Sampled HR@10 measures ranking against the pinned 99 negatives; it does not establish full-catalog superiority, because sampling can reverse model rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Recommended analysis: retain each user’s hit indicator for both models on identical candidates; compute paired differences and bootstrap users within each category, preserving pairs, then average the four category differences equally. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on these candidates and trained checkpoints; they exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling variability.

Repeated checkpoint and hyperparameter selection can overfit finite validation data ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Predeclare equal validation frequency, checkpoint-selection rules, and search budgets across objectives; record every attempted configuration and validation query. Treat selected-checkpoint intervals as descriptive, not selection-adjusted evidence. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged. For compute comparisons, report measured GPU-seconds alongside optimizer steps, sequences, and supervised target counts: equal epochs alone do not equalize masking supervision or computational cost.

[BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) learns masked-item reconstruction using bidirectional context. Recommended standardized diagnostics: evaluate both models on identical frozen training-only probes, with separate interior-mask and terminal-mask panels. Match users, target items, sequence truncation, corruption rules, and candidate sets within each panel; prevent target leakage. Gather features at actual supervised positions, excluding padding and unmasked tokens. Report per-target cross-entropy and ranking metrics with explicit denominators, plus per-user averages so long histories do not dominate. Terminal probes must reproduce appended-mask inference and left padding; use the final nonpadding position, never count−1. Report panels separately because interior probes have right context while terminal probes do not.
